newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures end stronger boosted by heating oi.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures end stronger boosted by heating oi.

text.p: IPE oil futures ended sharply higher as a cold weather lead rally in NYMEX heating oil boosted crude and products futures on both sides of the Atlantic on Monday, traders said.
Feb Brent shot up over $1.00 a barrel as forecasts for prolonged cold in several U.S. regions boosted NYMEX heating oil by over 3-1/2 cents a gallon and pegged gas oil $8.75 higher at the close.
Jan Brent expired at the close of business 57 cents up at $24.10 a barrel with Feb $95 cents up at $23.85 a barrel both sold off the highs at the close.
As Feb Brent strengthened sharply so the Jan/Feb backwardation narrowed, from around 50 cents in early business into around 12 cents before settling at 25 cents at the close.
Traders said forecasts that the cold weather could last well into January had prompted some hefty short-covering and fund buying against the Feb contract.
The American Petroleum Institute said at Dec 6 heating oil stocks were 12.6 million barrels below year ago levels.
Jan gas oil ended at $222.50, just off the high of $222.75, surprising some traders who saw little fundamental or technical support for the rally in Europe, that outpaced Friday's $8.50 gain.
"It's fund buying," said one trader, adding bulls had taken note of forecasts of cold weather in the U.S. Northeast and Mid-West that continue to fuel a rally in NYMEX futures.
Cold weather hit much of the central United States Monday on the heels of a storm that piled more than foot of snow on the upper Midwest.
